plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value: any deviation can only reduce expected profit. Overbidding risks losing money if tie-breaking or discrete steps interact; underbidding risks losing when I should profit. With value 49 and 0.1 increments, bidding 49 maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. I will bid exactly 49 to win whenever opponents’ top value is below 49 and pay the second-highest bid, yielding profit 49 − second-highest. ]

[ This is a private-values, independent-draw, second-price auction with rational opponents. In such auctions, bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks winning at a price exceeding my value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With 0.1 increments, bid exactly 44.0. No past rounds to update beliefs. Aim: win iff my value exceeds competitors’, paying their highest bid. ]

[ One-shot, sealed-bid, second-price auction with independent private values and rational opponents. In such auctions, truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks paying more than value; underbidding risks losing positive-surplus wins. With value 22, bid exactly 22 to win whenever second-highest bid is below 22 and pay that amount, ensuring nonnegative surplus when winning. ]
